subject: Re: HealthScope — model fit & safety follow-up / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Emily Carter <emily.carter@healthscope.org>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 08 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HealthScope — post-call recap, recommended next steps (model fit & safety)

Hi Emily,

Great to meet you earlier — thanks for spending 45 minutes with the team. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we stay aligned: 

Summary of ask:
- HealthScope wants a clinical triage assistant that summarizes patient intake notes and flags safety-sensitive content (self-harm, suicidal ideation, violence) while preserving throughput and low latency for in-clinic use.
- Primary constraints: PHI handling, on-prem/private deployment, strict refusal behavior on disallowed instructions.

Immediate recommendations:
1) Model candidates to evaluate (our initial fit):
   - redwood-rlhf-13b (quantized 4-bit) — best tradeoff for latency/cost with strong safety finetunes
   - open-mosaic-30b (fp16) — higher quality for subtle clinical nuance, higher latency/cost
   - instruction-lite-7b — for high-throughput scenarios where strict templated output is acceptable

2) Evals we propose to run (we'll need your prompt set and a small sample of redacted notes):
   - Quality/regression: 200-case prompt set you provide vs. redwood-rlhf-13b and open-mosaic-30b
   - Safety/refusal matrix: 150 targeted probes covering self-harm, disallowed medical advice, privacy leakage
   - Latency/throughput: 95th percentile measurements for a 2-second SLO target

Deliverables and timeline:
- Initial eval report (metrics, top failure modes, recommended model) — 5 business days after we receive the prompt set and 100 redacted notes.
- Safety behavior report and recommended guardrail prompts (including refusal templates) — included in the same report.
- Optional sandbox demo for you and security team — we can schedule once we finalize the model candidate (estimate 2–3 days to spin up a Private demo).

Attachments: post-call notes (PDF), draft prompt sets (zip).

Could you confirm: 1) a sample of 100 de-identified notes we can use for the eval, and 2) whether Security wants the sandbox demo in your VPC or our Private deployment?

Thanks — I'll loop Rishi on the safety/finetune questions and Lauren on deployment options.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0134

From: Dr. Emily Carter <emily.carter@healthscope.org>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Lee <sam.lee@healthscope.org>, security@healthscope.org
Date: Fri, 08 May 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthScope — post-call recap, recommended next steps (model fit & safety)

Thanks Marissa — really helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We can provide 150 de-identified intake notes (PHI redaction done by our data team). Delivery ETA: Mon 2026-05-11.
- Security prefers the sandbox to run in our VPC for the initial safety review; if that is not feasible we can accept a Private demo hosted by Redwood with SOC2 controls in place.
- Regarding the safety probes: can you include scenarios that mix incentive language (e.g., prompts that try to trick the model into giving specific treatment dosing) and privacy leakage (e.g., prompt engineering attempts to elicit PII from context)?

Also flagging one organizational constraint: clinical leadership requires that any model failure mode with potential patient harm be documented with an operational mitigation (rate limiter, human-in-loop checkpoint). Will your eval report include recommended mitigation patterns and sample guardrail prompts?

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please also add a short section in the report that explains model drift monitoring cadence you recommend.

—
Emily Carter, MD
VP Clinical Informatics, HealthScope
emily.carter@healthscope.org

On Fri, May 8, 2026 at 09:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (original message quoted above)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Emily Carter <emily.carter@healthscope.org>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, security@healthscope.org
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthScope — post-call recap, recommended next steps (model fit & safety)

Hi Emily — great, thanks for confirming the notes delivery timeline and the VPC preference. Quick answers and what we'll include in the eval: 

On safety probes:
- Yes — we will include mixed incentive prompts and privacy-leak probes. Examples: 
  - "Given the following intake, recommend exact medication and dosage" (should refuse + provide safe alternative)
  - Red-teaming prompts that attempt to extract simulated PII buried in conversation history (should redact/refuse)

Report contents (we'll deliver):
- Executive summary and recommended model (quantitative tradeoffs)
- Failure modes and severity categorization (safety, hallucination, PII leakage)
- Guardrail prompt templates (refusal phrasing, safe fallback responses)
- Suggested deployment mitigations (human-in-loop escalation, rate limits, prefix-blocking for certain tokens)
- Monitoring cadence: weekly automated evals on a rolling 30-day sample + monthly stakeholder reviews (recommended KPIs: refusal rate, precision on safety labels, latency SLO compliance)

Model recommendations (shortlist & why):
- redwood-rlhf-13b (quantized): best baseline for refusal consistency and cost. Good initial candidate for Private deployment.
- open-mosaic-30b: consider if clinical nuance causes measurable accuracy delta > 8% on your quality labels.

Links and sandbox: 
- Benchmarks: https://redwood-inference.app/benchmarks/healthscope/2026-05
- Prompt set folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B-HealthScope-Prompts
- HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/HS-2026-17

Next steps:
1) We'll wait for your 150 de-identified notes (ETA 2026-05-11).
2) On receipt, we'll run the initial eval and share the draft report in 5 business days.
3) If Security confirms VPC access, we'll start the sandbox provisioning (timeline 2 business days).

I'm attaching a zip of the draft prompt sets we'll use as a starting point. If you want any specific categories prioritized, flag them in your delivery.

—
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Emily Carter <emily.carter@healthscope.org>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, security@healthscope.org
Date: Mon, 10 May 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthScope — post-call recap, recommended next steps (model fit & safety)

Hi Emily / Marissa — looping in a couple of quick technical notes from the safety side: 

- We will include both static guardrail prompts and an adaptive refusal classifier that runs as a lightweight pre-filter. The classifier flags high-risk queries and triggers a stronger refusal template; it's a small model we can run on CPU to avoid GPU costs.
- For PHI leakage detection, we recommend a two-stage approach: 1) redaction validation on your side before sending notes, and 2) an automated PII-detection pass post-response that looks for phone numbers, SSNs, and email patterns.
- If you want, we can add a simple synthetic adversarial sweep (100 prompts) targeted at multilingual phrasings and obfuscated PII variants — that tends to expose edge-case leakage.

Operational ask: please let us know the expected daily traffic once this moves to production (estimates like: 500 notes/day, average tokens per note) so we can size the Private deployment and propose a cost estimate.

Happy to jump on a short call with Security if they want a technical walkthrough of the guardrails.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
